lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 127, for issue 126: tabs opened with -t and -T now use the saved sort.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one twenty-seven, for issue one twenty-six: tabs opened with dash t and dash capital T now use the saved sort.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
One added line makes a new folder view record its sort as soon as it is created, not when it is first drawn.
With this PR, the command creates tab A, and its file list is sorted by the saved sort, here Name.
The new line makes the view remember that sort right away.
Tab B asks the current tab for its sort, and now gets Name, even though tab A isn't on screen yet.
So every tab lists a, m, z in name order, and the Name header shows the sort arrow.
Before this PR, a view remembered its sort only when it was first drawn, and tab A wasn't drawn yet.
So it reported column 0, which is Date Created, a column that is hidden by default.
lines.say: So it reported column zero, which is Date Created, a column that is hidden by default.

lines.caption: Tab B sorted oldest first, and no visible header showed a sort arrow, so the list looked unsorted.
A new tab copies the sort of the current tab. With -t and -T, several tabs open before any is drawn.
lines.say: A new tab copies the sort of the current tab. With dash t and dash capital T, several tabs open before any is drawn.

lines.caption: The file list was always sorted right. Only the remembered copy that other tabs read was late, and it held Date Created.
The new line runs before the view listens for sort changes, so it never overwrites your saved sort.
The old place that stored the sort was the view's first draw, and with -t the next tab came first.
lines.say: The old place that stored the sort was the view's first draw, and with dash t the next tab came first.

lines.caption: Here is the change: one call to an existing function, right after the view applies its starting sort.
It is in the view's constructor, so it covers every way a tab is made. Only the -t and -T path was tested.
lines.say: It is in the view's constructor, so it covers every way a tab is made. Only the dash t and dash capital T path was tested.

lines.caption: The same call at first draw is now redundant, and is kept so the file stays close to upstream Thunar.
The PR changes one source line, adds a test script, and adds this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert this PR. It adds no setting.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The building session and CI each built it and ran all 24 tests. The latest commit hasn't been through CI yet.
lines.say: The building session and CI each built it and ran all twenty-four tests. The latest commit hasn't been through CI yet.

lines.caption: The reference is the first tab and new windows, which already use the saved sort.
The test's files are created in reverse name order, so Name puts a.txt first, and Date Created puts z.txt first.
lines.say: The test's files are created in reverse name order, so Name puts a dot t x t first, and Date Created puts z dot t x t first.

lines.caption: The test makes six folders, and stops early if the filesystem doesn't record distinct creation times.
It saves Name ascending as the sort, then opens three tabs in each of two panes.
In every tab it selects the first row, copies and pastes it, and requires a.txt. An empty paste fails clearly.
lines.say: In every tab it selects the first row, copies and pastes it, and requires a dot t x t. An empty paste fails clearly.

lines.caption: It takes a screenshot of the last tab in each pane, showing name order and the Name arrow. CI numbers them 29 and 30.
lines.say: It takes a screenshot of the last tab in each pane, showing name order and the Name arrow. CI numbers them twenty-nine and thirty.

lines.caption: In the building session's cloud container, the PR built and all 24 tests passed.
lines.say: In the building session's cloud container, the PR built and all twenty-four tests passed.

lines.caption: The new test passed in 27 seconds, and the older test for -t and -T tabs passed in 19.
lines.say: The new test passed in twenty-seven seconds, and the older test for dash t and dash capital T tabs passed in nineteen.

lines.caption: CI built it, and all 24 tests passed there. The new test took 26 seconds.
lines.say: CI built it, and all twenty-four tests passed there. The new test took twenty-six seconds.

lines.caption: An audit of all 214 CI screenshots found every one OK.
lines.say: An audit of all two hundred fourteen CI screenshots found every one OK.

lines.caption: The latest commit restores the draw-time call, and has not been through CI yet.
The birth-time guard was added after that run. CI's verify job ran it, and it passed.
Not run: the test against the old build, and the View, Sort By menu.
Also not run: folder-specific sort settings, and restoring tabs at startup.
Before the first push, a fresh agent reviewed the branch at level high and found 5 problems; 1 is fixed.
lines.say: Before the first push, a fresh agent reviewed the branch at level high and found five problems; one is fixed.

lines.caption: The test could have passed by luck where files have no creation time. It now fails early there.
The rest were skipped: this page came later, the redundant call stays, and CI's review later replaced the copied helpers.
CI's review found 11 problems over two reviews.
lines.say: CI's review found eleven problems over two reviews.

lines.caption: CI first removed the draw-time call, then suggested restoring it to match upstream. You chose to restore it, so it stays.
In the test, CI's findings brought the shared title helper, a clear message for an empty paste, and one unused line removed.
You accepted two code findings: cached sort values that stay in sync, and Trash's sort reaching a new tab, as upstream does.
You also accepted that the test takes 26 of its 120 seconds, and fails on purpose without birth times.
lines.say: You also accepted that the test takes twenty-six of its hundred and twenty seconds, and fails on purpose without birth times.

lines.caption: Two later low findings were accepted: a looser title match, and a failure path that exits anyway.
Your own script on real folders runs only once you install the next build.
The PR, the issue and CI's screenshots are linked here.
CI's review findings and the screenshot audit are linked too.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on 126. This is a standalone fix.
lines.say: No open issue depends on one twenty-six. This is a standalone fix.

lines.caption: In short: tabs opened together from the command line now sort by your saved sort, with the arrow on the right header.
